definition: A supplemental schedule used to report farm income and farm business expenses for individuals, estates, trusts, and partnerships engaged in farming activities, including both cash and accrual method accounting.

includes.text: Reports farm income using cash method accounting
Reports farm business expenses and deductions
Reports farm income using accrual method accounting
Calculates the net this document operations

excludes.text: Reports rental income from real property not materially participated in by the taxpayer
Reports employee business expenses and reimbursements
Reports profit or loss from self-employment business activities other than farming
excludes.quote: Schedule C (Form 1040) - Profit or Loss From Business

discriminators.text: Specifically designed for farming and agricultural activities with farm-specific income lines and expense categories; the sibling reports rental income from real property and passive activities
Reports business income and expenses from farming operations; the sibling reports employee business expenses and reimbursements for work-related costs
Dedicated to farming businesses with agricultural activity codes and farm-specific deductions; the sibling reports profit or loss from non-farm self-employment business activities
